executor_side_live_from_next_report: every quantitative claim in a boundary report carries computed: YES | NO. A claim marked NO may not be used as a reason for anything, only as a thing to check. The sentence that caused this node would have read 'all three choices happen to give the same verdicts here [computed: NO]'
declarer_side: any ruling resting on a premise from the executor's report names that premise and states whether it was verified; unverified premises make the ruling conditional
header_enumeration: now carries the FIRST and LAST ruling number of the immediately preceding node, so two internally consistent transmissions cannot collide — this would have caught both renumberings
standing_requirement: compute-don't-predict is now standing rather than per-node: A206 required computing rather than predicting for reasons unrelated to A205, and computing is what exposed A205's premise — a ruling caught the error in the ruling beside it
